Parser test fixture.

sourceAudit.notes: Path patterns match repository-relative paths at the audited commit. An asterisk can span directory separators. Groups can overlap when a file supports more than one workflow.

sourceGroups.reason: The installation guide gives the versioned GHCR image and mount point. Image manifests were checked for linux/386, linux/amd64 and linux/arm64. A container runtime was unavailable for execution.

sourceGroups.topic: Source builds, releases, and contribution automation
sourceGroups.reason: Install, contribute, and coverage guides cover the reader workflows. Build recipes, workflow internals, and issue form schemas are upstream maintenance configuration.

sourceGroups.topic: XGo CLI and shell-facing command help
sourceGroups.reason: The command and environment guides cover command flags, package versus file mode, root and compiler selection, and module settings. Backend internals are implementation evidence.
The guide demonstrates file layout, generated output, check mode, and collisions using a reader-owned project.

sourceGroups.topic: HDQ executable and registered data fetchers
sourceGroups.reason: The toolchain guide demonstrates building the standalone command, listing fetch types and extracting links from URLs or standard input. A Go example registers a converter and applies it to saved HTML through fetcher.From. The deprecated library has a migration guide.
The source inspection guide demonstrates parsing an in-memory file, walking identifiers, reporting original positions and formatting the syntax tree.

sourceGroups.topic: Converting Go and XGo syntax trees and querying compatibility nodes
sourceGroups.reason: The inspection guide covers declaration conversion limits, an in-memory mixed package, direct imports and XGo standard-library path normalization. The compatibility query API remains an advanced topic.

sourceGroups.topic: Mixed Go and XGo type checking
sourceGroups.reason: Tooling conventions cover configuration and the information model. The package loading guide demonstrates resolving a Go call to an XGo declaration and collecting diagnostics.

sourceGroups.topic: Programmatic compilation, package loading, and documentation outlines
sourceGroups.reason: The source inspection guide demonstrates in-memory compilation. The package loading guide demonstrates loading a package from its module directory and restoring XGo overload names in Go documentation data.
CLI watch and server launch plus VS Code setup describe the user workflow. The watcher, JSON-RPC, and stdio packages provide integration code.

sourceGroups.topic: DQL adapters and domain text encodings
sourceGroups.reason: Reference and demo pages cover the query model, built-in adapters, domain literals, and the custom NodeSet contract. The package implementations are source evidence.

The Go embedding guide demonstrates grammar compilation, list flattening, error positions, expression, file and prefix matching, and a custom scanner that filters inserted semicolons. Position relocation and AST construction helpers remain available in the source.
The generated builtin declaration file provides signatures and comments for the existing builtins, strings, and collections references. The compiler registration file governs availability.
The reference shows how to run the grammar checker and explains its syntax-only scope with accepted and rejected inputs.
The classfile guide explains the test framework. The demo and coverage pages show how to run tests and measure coverage.
All tracked demo paths have site source records. Runtime coverage varies by toolchain and platform, as noted on demo pages.

sourceGroups.topic: Compiler fixtures, goldens, and Go unit tests
sourceGroups.reason: Reader-facing semantics such as decorators, automatic closures, type arguments and initialized allocation have runnable examples. Other fixtures and expected compiler output support regression testing.
The Mini Specification guide covers running the checker. Other generators and test helpers maintain upstream artifacts.
The generated artifacts follow their authored XGo sources. Demo pages can show generated Go where needed to explain interoperability.
The current upstream Markdown has no references to these images. The domain literal reference and design article cover this topic in text.

sourceGroups.topic: Repository metadata and dependency lock files
sourceGroups.reason: License information is cited through the source disclosure. Git settings and dependency lock files are build inputs.

The interpreter and host guides cover CLI and REPL startup, basic XGo embedding, and optional adapters. Package export, advanced CLI flags, and the patched Go runtime workflow remain separate candidate topics.

The host guide demonstrates package export registration and use of a bundled direct-call adapter, plus the aggregate import and logging exception. The regeneration workflow concerns maintenance of the upstream bundles.
The Go host calls a stateful interpreted closure by registering its exact signature. The guide also covers built-in signatures, reflection fallback, and the registration lifetime.

The Go host runs identical recursion in separate contexts with the memoization plugin enabled and disabled. The guide covers eligibility and floating-point behavior. Upstream benchmark figures and contributor tests describe the upstream test environment.
